notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Financial figures are from the FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000831001-25-000067) and match SEC XBRL. Ownership is from the 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A filed March 18, 2025, accession 0001145443-25-000075). LEADER: Jane Fraser beneficially owned 270,038 shares at March 3, 2025, less than 1% (the proxy states no director or executive officer owned more than 1%), so pctEconomic is null. Her 'Total Ownership' column of 626,418 adds 356,380 shares of deferred receipt, which are not counted as beneficially owned. HOLDERS: both 5% rows rely on Schedule 13G/A filings from early 2024 (BlackRock filed January 25, 2024; Vanguard filed February 13, 2024); the proxy gives only filing dates, so asOf is null. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow statement reports one 'Dividends paid' line covering common and preferred dividends ($5,199 million). The 10-K separately says 'In 2024, Citi repurchased $2.5 billion of common shares and paid $4.2 billion of common dividends'; the equity statement shows common dividends of $4,218 million and preferred dividends of $1,054 million declared. BUYBACKS: 'Treasury stock acquired' of $2,474 million is common stock; the $5,050 million redemption of preferred stock is excluded. STOCK COMP: null. Citi does not state one company-wide share-based compensation expense. Its incentive compensation cost table (Note 7, total $2,130 million in 2024) mixes stock and cash awards: charges for estimated awards to retirement-eligible employees $741 million (stock and cash), amortization of deferred cash awards, deferred cash stock units and performance stock units $186 million, immediately vested stock award expense $130 million, amortization of restricted and deferred stock awards $718 million, other variable incentive compensation $355 million. The related income tax benefits for stock-based compensation were $428 million. Summing the stock lines would be a derivation, so the value is left null. PLAN: no employee stock purchase plan is described in the 10-K. GEOGRAPHY: 'North America' primarily reflects the U.S.; 'Corporate/Other' largely reflects U.S. activities and intersegment eliminations; U.K. revenues were about $6.7 billion within International (10-K footnotes).

footprint.notes: State rows are the FDIC Summary of Deposits, June 30, 2024 survey, for Citibank, N.A. (cert 7213), aggregated server-side by the FDIC BankFind API by branch state. Citibank has SOD offices in 12 states plus DC. FDIC totals for the query: 657 offices and $743,363,000 thousand. Deposits follow booking office: South Dakota (main office, Sioux Falls) shows 2 offices with $463.9 billion, and Texas 2 offices with $30.8 billion, which reflect where deposits are booked, not where depositors are. Delaware shows 1 office with $0 deposits. Puerto Rico (2 offices) is in the FDIC response but is not a state; omitted. Regions: the 10-K human capital table splits ~229,000 employees into North America 86k and International 143k (Mexico in International; by business and region, not physical residence); the 10-K gives no country breakdown and no list of the region's countries. 10-K Item 2 Properties reads 'Not Applicable', so the only site is the headquarters from the cover page. Citi's per-country websites were not used (no consistent dated set).
